Needs changes before merge.

The new guards refuse a G86 dwell by name on all five selected posts. The command checks reject a dwell outside the stated range. The changes use the existing command and undo paths.

I reviewed this safety-tier change locally after a trial merge with upstream/main at e3f7d122b3c7fb86aff4c893667f02378fc707d8. The merge had no conflicts. I used the current upstream AGENTS.md. I did not use a GitHub runner.

Results:
- The app `bore_cycle` test target does not compile. No app bore tests ran.
- The post `bore_cycle` suite has 5 passed tests and 2 failed tests.
- The existing `ream_cycle` suites pass: 3 app tests and 5 post tests.
- Clippy passes with `-D warnings` for both libraries and for all post targets.
- The combined app/post all-target Clippy check fails in `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs:106`. That unchanged upstream fixture has an obsolete `CuttingRow` initializer. This is a separate upstream fault.
- I read all six new NC golden files line by line. No existing golden file changes.
- Mutation 1: I disabled the Fanuc G86 dwell guard. The refusal test failed. I restored the guard, and the test passed.
- Mutation 2: I disabled the Haas G86 dwell guard. The refusal test failed. I restored the guard, and the test passed.

Requested before merge:
1. `crates/app/tests/bore_cycle.rs:50`: Add `break_through: None` to the `OpParams::Drill` fixture. Current main requires this field. Then run all three app bore tests. The compiler reports:
   ```text
   error[E0063]: missing field `break_through` in initializer of `OpParams`
   ```
2. `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs:183`: Change the expanded-bore test to match the safety refusal on current main. Heidenhain, TinyG and Carvera now refuse a bore because they cannot stop the spindle before the rapid retract. The test fails at its first Heidenhain call. Check the named refusal and the absence of cutting output. Remove the unsafe Heidenhain golden expectation from `GOLDEN`. Update the body and decision record to describe the refusal. Do not restore the unsafe expansion. The diagnostic is:
   ```text
   operation Bore: bore (G86) requires a spindle stop before rapid retract - expanded boring is not supported by this post; refused, not posted
   ```
3. `crates/post/tests/golden/bore/fanuc.nc:12`: Update the new NC goldens against current main, after item 2. The byte comparison fails because main now writes decimal points on coordinate words. For example, the golden has `G00 Z10`, but the post writes `G00 Z10.`. Check each regenerated line and run the complete post bore suite.

The new post refusal test detects both tested guard removals. The app validation tests still need execution after the fixture fix. No UI screenshot requirement applies. No real control ran this output.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: Findings 1 and 3 are fixed in a local held commit. Finding 2 is blocked. No changes were pushed.

- Finding 1: Added `break_through: None` to the app fixture. All three app `bore_cycle` tests pass. Removing the field gives compiler error E0063. Restoring it gives GREEN.
- Finding 3: Regenerated and inspected all five supported NC goldens. Only Fanuc and Haas need decimal coordinate changes. `the_named_posts_post_the_bore_byte_exact` fails with the old goldens and passes with the restored goldens.
- Finding 2: Replaced the unsafe expansion expectation with `expanding_posts_refuse_a_bore_by_name_without_cutting_output`. Removed the Heidenhain golden. The new pin fails on current main. Heidenhain reports the named refusal, but still emits `N100 G01 X+10 Y+10 Z-12 F120*` and a second bore cut. The `BORE` refusal branch in `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` returns, but the engine continues through the cutting chain. I did not change production logic or weaken this pin.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is RED: 153 of 154 steps pass. Only the new no-cut refusal pin fails. The post bore suite has 6 passed tests and 1 failed test. The app bore suite has 3 passed tests. Clippy passes for all app and post targets with `-D warnings`.

The local held commit is `0516501755c32d29739d0ea085e2e65345975662` on branch `fix-1821`. It includes a clean merge of upstream main `4e0b9abefcb225595d47d9c69a2482d6359b190f`.
The remote PR head remains `1c06a3e1e37d53b7a48d3e27708eb8b2b0190f27`.

The resolve-conflicts skill says to stop when a failure is in main code. Please re-review finding 2 and this blocking evidence. No label was removed.

This PR goes back to draft. The review of head `1c06a3e1e` has the label `needs-rework`. A rework agent fixes the three requested items now. The PR gets no push while it is ready, so it is a draft first.

Rework of the review of head `1c06a3e1e`. The new head is `7e6629ad1`.

The branch has a merge of `origin/main`. The merge was clean. It is needed because the findings exist only on current main.

- Item 1 (app fixture): done. `break_through: None` is in the `OpParams::Drill` fixture. The three app bore tests pass.
- Item 2 (expanded bore test): done. The test now checks the by-name refusal on heidenhain, tinyg and carvera, with and without a dwell. It also checks that no G86 and no dwell block is written. The Heidenhain golden and its `GOLDEN` entry are removed. The decision record and the PR body describe the refusal.
- Item 3 (goldens): done. `fanuc.nc` and `haas.nc` are regenerated. I read the diff: the only change is the decimal point on coordinate words. The sinumerik, grblhal and tormach goldens did not change.

Note: a refusal on these posts is the counted warning. The host blocks the post on it. The program text still holds the plain feed and rapid moves of the bore, as on main. I did not assert that those moves are absent.

Gate: `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test bore_cycle`: 7 passed. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test bore_cycle`: 3 passed.

Not exercised: the quick gate tier, clippy, the `ream_cycle` suites, the unchanged `wire_tool.rs` fixture fault. No real control ran this output.

The PR stays a draft.

Addressed: all three findings from the latest review.

- Finding 1: The app drill fixture includes `break_through: None`. All four app `bore_cycle` tests pass. Removing the field fails compilation with E0063. Restoring it passes.
- Finding 2: Heidenhain, TinyG and Carvera have named refusal checks with and without dwell. The unsafe Heidenhain golden is removed. The new app test `refused_expanded_bores_write_no_nc_file` proves that the app refuses the program and writes no NC file for all six cases. Bypassing the app warning gate makes this test fail; restoring it passes. Rejected engine text can still contain fallback moves, as the maintainer noted. The decision record and PR body explain this boundary. No unsafe expansion was restored.
- Finding 3: The Fanuc and Haas goldens contain decimal coordinate words. I inspected all five goldens. `the_named_posts_post_the_bore_byte_exact` fails with the old goldens and passes after restoration. The complete post bore suite passes all seven tests.

Head: `dbee7b8e8da4ab76df525dd93b697fde050b79d1`.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 154 steps and 0 failed. App/post all-target Clippy: GREEN with `-D warnings`.

The PR remains a draft. Please re-review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: dbee7b8e8da4ab76df525dd93b697fde050b79d1 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

All three findings from the earlier review are met:
- The app drill fixture has `break_through: None`. All four app bore tests pass.
- Heidenhain, TinyG and Carvera have named refusal checks, with and without dwell. The app test checks all six cases and confirms that no NC file is written. The unsafe Heidenhain golden is removed. The body and decision record explain that rejected engine text can still contain fallback moves. The app warning check blocks that text before file output.
- The Fanuc and Haas goldens have decimal coordinate words. I read all five NC goldens line by line. The complete post bore suite passes.

This is a safety-tier review. I used the current upstream/main AGENTS.md. I tested locally in an isolated worktree after a clean trial merge with upstream/main at d2b8d0c6be57f6bff8b444addccf872cb0bcf325. No GitHub runner was used.

Results:
- Build: `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --test bore_cycle --test ream_cycle --no-run` passed.
- App `bore_cycle`: 4 passed, 0 failed.
- Post `bore_cycle`: 7 passed, 0 failed.
- App `ream_cycle`: 3 passed, 0 failed.
- Post `ream_cycle`: 5 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- The quick gate plan was read with `--dry-run`. The full quick gate was not run. The tests above were selected directly for this change.
- The first build attempt made no progress with the compile cache. I stopped it and ran the build and checks with the cache disabled.

I ran these mutation checks myself:
1. Restored the obsolete Fanuc golden: the byte comparison test failed. Restored the current golden: the test passed.
2. Bypassed the app warning check: `refused_expanded_bores_write_no_nc_file` failed because posting returned an NC program. Restored the check: the test passed for all six cases. The temporary NC file was removed.
3. Disabled the Fanuc G86 dwell guard: the named refusal test failed. Restored the guard: the test passed.

All temporary changes were restored. No changes are requested before merge. No UI screenshot requirement applies. No real control ran this output. The PR author is NeoTech, so this review leaves the draft state unchanged.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
